title: A passing make ci leaves no build a sibling can pin
foundBy: user report (host): "it doesn't seem possible anymore to have make repin do pin on local builds, which haven't been published to ghcr.io or npmjs.com or built in the Github CI builds"

evidence.verified: `make ci` at 7f94c70 ended `record-build: recorded dashboards 7f94c70 as a local build in ~/.local/share/cs-builds/codesweep-ai (go v0.0.0-20260926051938-7f94c705329b)`. tests/test_record_build.py passes all 15 of its tests against this same scripts/record-build.sh, byte for byte. GitHub CI's `ci` passed on 7f94c70.

resolution: A clean, passing `make ci` now records its commit in the owner's build store, `~/.local/share/cs-builds/<owner>/`. It keeps the Go module in the module proxy's layout, the npm packages where the project has them, and an entry naming the versions. A run over uncommitted changes records nothing, and says so.
details: `make ci` runs every gate CI runs, on this machine, and leaves nothing another project can pin. Pins move only to commits GitHub CI lists as built. So a change across several projects has to be pushed and built one project at a time before the next can pin it. A clean passing run could record its commit as a local build instead: the module zip Go resolves it from, and an entry naming its versions. They would go in a store the sibling projects read. Go and npm builds of a clean commit are byte-identical to CI's. A pin on such a build is therefore the pin CI writes once that commit is pushed. SPEC.md describes the status file every project publishes, and would describe that store's layout beside it.
